Shape Constraints for a Smooth

Source: R/shape.R
shape_constructors.Rd

Construct the shapes that scs() imposes on a smooth. shape_increasing() and shape_decreasing() give a monotone curve, with a slope of at least min_slope in absolute value; shape_convex() and shape_concave() give a curve of constant sign of curvature.

Usage

shape_increasing(link = linkfunctions7::log_link(), min_slope = 0)

shape_decreasing(link = linkfunctions7::log_link(), min_slope = 0)

shape_convex(link = linkfunctions7::log_link())

shape_concave(link = linkfunctions7::log_link())

Arguments

link

A linkfunctions7 link onto \((0, \infty)\), by default linkfunctions7::log_link(). linkfunctions7::softplus_link() is the other shipped choice.

min_slope

A single nonnegative number, the smallest slope in absolute value.

Value

An S7 object of class ShapeMonotone (shape_increasing(), shape_decreasing()) or ShapeCurvature (shape_convex(), shape_concave()), both inheriting from shape_constraint.

Details

A monotone shape parametrizes the slopes of the B-spline coefficients on the Greville abscissae, \(s_j = \pm(\delta + g^{-1}(\gamma_j))\) with \(\delta\) = min_slope. A curvature shape keeps the slope at the left end free and parametrizes the second divided differences, \(\pm g^{-1}(\gamma_j)\). See shape_constraint for the map.

See also

scs(), shape_constraint.

Examples

shape_increasing()
#> <shape: increasing, link = log>
shape_decreasing(min_slope = 0.1)
#> <shape: decreasing, link = log, min_slope = 0.1>
shape_convex(link = linkfunctions7::softplus_link())
#> <shape: convex, link = softplus(a=1)>

# A link onto the whole real line is rejected.
try(shape_concave(link = linkfunctions7::identity_link()))
#> Error : the link 'identity' maps onto (-Inf, Inf); a shape needs a link onto (0, Inf),
#>   such as log_link() or softplus_link().
